---
title: "CanadaLogin Signal Check"
subtitle: "For the two-week period of January 1-14"
author: "EDCP Data and Research Team"  # example@cds-snc.ca
date: "2026-01-15"
params:
  edition: 0
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    theme: [cosmo, _fonts.scss]   # _fonts.scss: self-hosted brand fonts
    toc: false
    fig-width: 8
    fig-height: 3.4
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

```{r setup}
# Style template. Built-in R datasets stand in for the frozen Athena queries,
# so it renders without an AWS session. In a real edition, every query lives
# here, inline, under its figure's header, and the figure chunks only plot.
source("../R/connection.R")
source("../R/branding.R")
source("../R/colours.R")
source("../R/publishing.R")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(scales)
})

# Every date is named once, here, as a hardcoded literal; derive the rest.
# Watermark date: the date this report is first created.
report_date <- as.Date("2026-01-15")

period_start <- as.Date("2026-01-01")
period_end <- period_start + 13

# Figure 1 --------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# The scale read: one series over time, latest point called out.
scale_series <- economics |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2010-01-01")) |>
  transmute(date, value = psavert)

scale_latest <- slice_max(scale_series, date, n = 1)

# Figure 2 --------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# A category comparison, with one newcomer highlighted.
categories <- mpg |>
  count(manufacturer, name = "n") |>
  slice_max(n, n = 8) |>
  mutate(is_new = manufacturer == "audi")

newcomer <- filter(categories, is_new)

# Figure 3 --------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# A stacked series: a few groups in colour, everything else binned grey.
highlight_cities <- c("Houston", "Dallas", "Austin")

monthly_sales <- txhousing |>
  filter(year == 2014, !is.na(sales)) |>
  mutate(
    month_end = as.Date(paste(year, month, 1, sep = "-")),
    group = if_else(city %in% highlight_cities, city, "Other")
  ) |>
  group_by(month_end, group) |>
  summarise(sales = sum(sales), .groups = "drop")

peak_month <- monthly_sales |>
  group_by(month_end) |>
  summarise(sales = sum(sales), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(sales, n = 1)
```

This is the **CanadaLogin Signal Check**, our read on CanadaLogin every two
weeks. This edition covers three things: how far usage grew, how a new
service compares with the rest, and one more story from the period.

**Each paragraph opens with its takeaway, not its topic.** The bolded action
title is one short clause a reader can skim. The body then carries what the
figure cannot, and bolds only the one or two numbers that prove the point: here,
the latest value of **`r scale_latest$value`%** on
`r format_long_date(scale_latest$date)`. The first figure is always the scale
read: how much CanadaLogin is used, and how that changed.

```{r figure-1}
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Line chart of US personal savings rate from 2010 to 2015, a placeholder
#|   for the scale read. The final point is highlighted in red with its value.

scale_plot <- ggplot(scale_series, aes(date, value)) +
  geom_line(color = colors$brand["blue"], linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = scale_latest, color = colors$brand["red"], size = 3.2) +
  geom_text(
    data = scale_latest, aes(label = paste0(value, "%")),
    color = colors$brand["red"], vjust = -1, fontface = "bold", size = 3.6
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  theme_cds() +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Savings rate (%)",
    title = "Titles state the takeaway, as the paragraph does",
    subtitle = "Subtitles state the measure, the source, and the date range."
  )

add_cds_logo(add_watermark(scale_plot, date = report_date,
                           edition = params$edition))
```

**A newcomer is easier to judge beside its peers.** Highlight the new entry
in brand orange and label every bar, so no reader has to estimate from the
axis. Here the newcomer has **`r newcomer$n`** models.

```{r figure-2}
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Horizontal bar chart of model counts for the eight largest manufacturers
#|   in the mpg dataset, a placeholder for a service comparison. Bars are brand
#|   blue with one highlighted in orange, and every bar carries its value.

category_plot <- ggplot(categories, aes(n, reorder(manufacturer, n),
                                        fill = is_new)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(n)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      `TRUE` = unname(colors$brand_action["orange"]),
      `FALSE` = unname(colors$brand["blue"])
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = comma, limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))
  ) +
  theme_cds() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()) +
  labs(
    x = "Models", y = NULL,
    title = "The newcomer sits mid-pack",
    subtitle = "Model count by manufacturer (mpg dataset)."
  )

add_cds_logo(add_watermark(category_plot, date = report_date,
                           edition = params$edition))
```

**Name a few groups and let the rest fall back to grey.** When many series
compete, colour only the ones the paragraph talks about. Sales peaked at
**`r comma(peak_month$sales)`** in
`r format(peak_month$month_end, "%B")`. A taller figure needs its logo
height scaled so the logo stays the same size on the page.

```{r figure-3}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-alt: |
#|   Stacked bar chart of monthly home sales in Texas in 2014, a placeholder
#|   for a daily series with a few groups picked out. Houston, Dallas and
#|   Austin are in colour and all other cities are one grey band.

group_labels <- c(
  Houston = "Houston", Dallas = "Dallas", Austin = "Austin",
  Other = "All other cities"
)
group_colours <- c(
  Houston = unname(colors$brand["orange"]),
  Dallas = unname(colors$brand["red"]),
  Austin = unname(colors$brand["blue"]),
  Other = unname(colors$brand["grey"])
)

stacked_plot <- ggplot(
  # The first level stacks on top, so the grey band caps each bar.
  mutate(monthly_sales, group = factor(group, rev(names(group_labels)))),
  aes(month_end, sales, fill = group)
) +
  geom_col(width = 25) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = group_colours, labels = group_labels,
    breaks = names(group_labels), name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma, limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b") +
  theme_cds() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.justification = "left",
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Sales per month",
    title = "Three cities carry most of the volume",
    subtitle = "Monthly home sales in Texas, 2014 (txhousing dataset)."
  )

# Taller figure, so the logo height fraction is scaled to match the others.
add_cds_logo(
  add_watermark(stacked_plot, date = report_date, edition = params$edition),
  height = 0.13 * 3.4 / 5
)
```
